cause: D3DX converts 8-bit source channels to A4R4G4B4/R5G6B5/A1R5G5B5 textures by rounding to the nearest code; the port truncated, so ascii.anm (format 5) text was exactly one 4-bit step (+/-17) off. Fixed in both the 32-bit (original_texture_rgba) and 16-bit (color565::texture) paths; R5G6B5 framebuffer truncation unchanged.

campaign.criteria: channel tolerance 2, bad fraction <=1%, MAE <=1; no masks or alignment
campaign.simulation: scalar checkpoints equal in every case (unchanged by a texture-only fix)

different_value.explanation: original shows 59.88fps (real frame drop on the capture machine) where the port shows 60.00fps; different displayed value, excluded by the criteria

stage_first_frame.explanation: frame 1 of every stage: text over black (HUD not drawn yet); opaque texels identical, only glyph fringe pixels differ (original +2..+8 brighter); frame 2 is identical. Separate first-frame defect (what lies under the text on the stage-entry frame), not texture quantization

mae_over_3.region: playfield only in every case (HUD MAE 0.05, fps 0.02)
mae_over_3.classification: separate playfield rendering defect at the same stage moments across cases (stage 2 ~9000, stage 3 ~14400, stage 5 ~14400-16200); present before this fix and reduced by it (max 8.67 -> 7.81); not related to the fps counter

limits: Pixels were deleted after each case; the spike clusters are classified from region metrics, not from inspected images
Native macOS captures only; the wasm build shares the same conversion code
